recommendation: Keep the empty audit commit. If generated ShEx ever regresses to recursive primitive value shapes, fix the external Kindling/org.hl7.fhir.core ShEx generator used by the build rather than editing generated artifacts or duplicating prose in this checkout.
issue_request: FHIR-25619 was Published/Persuasive for R5 and reported that generated ShEx for FHIR primitive types was incorrect, using recursive primitive shapes such as fhir:value @<integer> where primitive values should be constrained by XML Schema datatypes.
initial_application: No HL7/fhir source commit explicitly tagged FHIR-25619 was found, and this checkout does not track the Java ShEx generator or generated primitive ShEx source files. Historical generated R4/R4B ShEx showed the reported problem, while R5 and current generated ShEx now use fhir:v with concrete XSD datatype constraints such as xsd:int plus the FHIR integer range.
additional_context: FHIR-I minutes for 2020-11-02 record the issue as a technical correction, auto-approved. The current build path invokes the Kindling publisher from build.gradle.kts, source/rdf.html documents primitive RDF values as fhir:v literals, and related ShEx issues FHIR-25620, FHIR-25621, and FHIR-25622 are already represented on the combined branch.
reconciliation: No source edit was made. The current generated ShEx surface already satisfies the issue intent; changing integer to bare xsd:integer would weaken the current xsd:int/min-max semantics for FHIR integer.
